# Kumārapetavatthu (Pv 30)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kumārapetavatthu* (Pv 30) is a narrative poem preserved in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Canon. The work addresses how one escapes an evil past, illustrating the torments experienced by beings in consequence of sinful deeds committed in previous lives [Law 1926], including the motif of adultery resulting in an unfortunate ghostly rebirth [Clark 1994]. A verse cited by Seishi Karashima (Pv 453) recounts the miraculous preservation of an infant abandoned in a charnel ground who is protected from dangerous beings and sustained by virtue of past merit (*katapuññakumāra*) [Karashima 2012].

**Sources**

- [Karashima 2012] Seishi Karashima, Abhisamācārikā Dharmāḥ: Verhaltensregeln für buddhistische Mönche der Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravādins (2012) — Cites verse Pv 453 regarding the abandoned baby in the charnel ground sustained by past merit.
- [Law 1926] Bimala Churn Law, Ancient Indian Tribes (1926) — Mentions the story of Kumarapeta in the context of post-mortem retribution for sinful deeds.
- [Clark 1994] Robert Warren Clark, Māra: Psychopathology and Evil in the Buddhism of India and Tibet (1994) — Notes the motif of adultery leading to unfortunate rebirth in the Kumārapeta account.
